chunks: And from him, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Qunut is [performed] in the Friday prayer, the evening prayer, the late night prayer, the Witr prayer, and the dawn prayer; so whoever leaves the Qunut out of preference (for not doing it), then his prayer is not valid.

key_terms.اَلْقُنُوتُ: Qunut: Supplication recited during prayer, considered a pillar or essential component in this context.
key_terms.رَغْبَةً عَنْهُ: Out of preference: Leaving something voluntarily because one prefers not to do it, as opposed to forgetting or being unable.
key_terms.فَلَا صَلَاةَ لَهُ: His prayer is not valid: A legal ruling indicating the prayer is void or incomplete due to the omission.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on leaving Qunut in specific prayers according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* underscores the high status of Qunut, distinguishing between mere omission and deliberate rejection (*raghbatan*), which invalidates the prayer. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that Qunut in these specific prayers is not merely recommended but carries the weight of a condition for the validity of the prayer when performed with intent. This ruling reflects the broader Shia emphasis on the spiritual and legal significance of supplication within the daily ritual structure.
